etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin mūsēum (“library, study”), from Ancient Greek Μουσεῖον (Mouseîon), shrine of the Muses (Μοῦσα (Moûsa)).

definitions.definition: A building or institution dedicated to the acquisition, conservation, study, exhibition, and educational interpretation of objects having scientific, historical, cultural or artistic value.
(transitive, intransitive) To place in a museum.

quote.citation: 2013, Jeanette Winterson, Art Objects: Essays on Ecstasy and Effrontery:
quote.text: I use daily those books that for others are museumed. The glass case approach depresses me, makes books into porcelain, guts them of what they are.

quote.citation: 2016, Pamela Erskine-Loftus, Mariam Ibrahim Al-Mulla, Victoria Hightower, Representing the Nation, page 77:
quote.text: Such museuming provides evidence that the Gulf has started building up its defences to protect its national culture, which might be seen as threatened by modern, global societies.
I told her I'd do just one visit to start; I don't really have time to do a lot of museuming.
